title: Come, Ye Who Love the Lord
description: Come, Ye Who Love the Lord in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 3, “Cheerful Worship”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, ye who love the Lord! And let your joys be known; Join in a song with sweet ac-cord, And thus sur-round His throne.

lines: Come, ye who love the Lord!
And let your joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
The sons of God have found
From faith and hope may grow.
We're travelling through the paths of peace

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
